text:
anna: Heads-up — staging p99 shot up after the tokenizer-normalize-mapping merge (PR #4823). CI perf test flagged a 2.6x p99 increase.

mike: saw that. Any obvious changelog? commit was the new normalization table + small kernel selector tweak in runtime.

priya: i ran the perf test locally — sequences are ~18% longer on average after token remap. KV cache hit rate drops and we start hitting the slower attention kernel at step ~120.

jonathan: can you paste the failing CI summary? perf-bot: CI perf check failed: gen_p99 320ms -> 840ms (+162%), kv_cache_hit_rate 0.87 -> 0.55, kernel_selector: preferred "fast-attn-v2" -> fallback "safe-attn" on some shards.

mike: fallback to safe-attn explains the latency but why did selector flip? selector logic picks kernel by expected seq len distribution + quant profile.

priya: the tokenizer table increased EOS token frequency for multi-byte characters; that shifts rolling sequence length sample. small change in the percentile estimator -> kernel threshold crossed.

tara: is this a config drift issue? new tokenizer PR modified tokenization without updating runtime's tokenizer-profile.json that the kernel selector uses.

anna: we didn't include a profile update in the model onboarding checklist. rollout was canary with 10% traffic, but canary autoscaler was small so noise amplified.

mike: repro steps I used:

```
# generate workload similar to CI
python tests/perf/run_gen.py --model rdinfer-v1.3 --profile tokenizer-sample-2026 --requests 5000
# capture kernel selection log
grep "kernel_selector" /tmp/runtime-debug.log | tail -n 50
```

jonathan: logs show repeated kernel flips per worker:

```
worker-7 kernel_selector: chosen=safe-attn reason=pred_seq_p99>128 (value=137)
worker-7 kv_cache: evict_count=42 hit_rate=0.62
worker-3 kernel_selector: chosen=fast-attn-v2 reason=pred_seq_p99<=128 (value=120)
```

priya: that causes batch heterogeneity — some batches use safe-attn (much slower) and some fast-attn, so p99 gets dominated by the tail.

tara: options:
- revert tokenizer remap PR (quick, but loses correctness fix)
- force kernel selector thresholds in runtime for this model (hotfix)
- update profile and run a shadow run + canary again

mike: I started a bisect-ish run across the merge range: 2762220400..2762223300 to see which commit nudged the percentile estimator. preliminary shows the runtime tweak combined with token map change is the combo.

anna: can we do a targeted rollback: revert runtime kernel selector tweak in canary only while leaving tokenizer change? that'd keep correctness in main but avoid the perf hit for users.

jonathan: that would require a config pin per deploy group. I can push a canary-only override: set kernel_selector.force_policy=stable for canary shards. patch: runtime/overrides/canary-kernel-pin.patch

priya: ran a quick patched shadow on staging with force_policy=stable -> p99 back to 360ms, kv_hit_rate 0.85. looks promising.

perf-bot: @anna created incident perf-2026-03-18-1, severity=minor, assigned=eng-runtime, notes="canary blocked by kernel flip after tokenizer-onboard".

tara: next steps — (1) hold the main rollout until we've updated the selector profile and validated shadow for 24h, (2) add tokenizer profile update to onboarding checklist, (3) follow up PR to adjust percentile estimator to be robust to small token-distribution shifts.

mike: i'll open the runtime revert PR for canary pin: https://git.internal/rdinfer/runtime/pull/4991

anna: thanks. prioritize the checklist change too — this felt like a two-team coordination gap.

jonathan: leaving notes for on-call: if you see kernel flips + kv eviction surge, set canary override and ping eng-runtime.

priya: posting flamegraph link from the patched run: https://perf.internal/redwood/2789/flame.svg — compare before/after. the safe-attn stack is huge in the before run.

mike: assigning follow-ups: PR 4991 (canary pin), PR 4992 (selector profile update), DOC 217 (onboarding checklist change).

anna: closing loop — revert/canary pin in 30m window, will monitor.

mike: :thumbsup:

jonathan: note — this was low-risk correctness change but big perf ripple. nice catch by CI perf tests.
